transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-23
Time: 09:00 PT / 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Verdance CTO), Samir Rao (Verdance ML Eng), Priya Nair (Verdance Security)

Summary:
Verdance Studio is evaluating Redwood for a rapid prototype and pilot. They're primarily interested in a PLG self-serve onramp but have regulatory constraints around customer data and want to understand hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem). Key asks: time-to-first-token, free credits for a 2-week sprint, SOC2/SSO/KMS details, and a simple benchmark plan for latency and cost.

Topics Covered:
- Quickstart / credits / time-to-first-token expectations
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC & on-prem) tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2, KMS, SSO, audit logs, data residency
- Pilot scope: perf benchmarks, sample prompts, success criteria
- Next steps and deliverables

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (AE): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — who we got?
[00:07] Lena (CTO): Hey, Lena here. Samir and Priya as well.
[00:10] Ethan (AE): Great. I'm Ethan, account lead, and Maya's the solutions engineer. We'll walk through how Redwood gets teams from zero to first token and what the pilot could look like.
[00:20] Maya (SE): Hey, all. Quick note — I'll focus on latency/cost and deployment patterns, happy to jump in.
[00:26] Lena (CTO): To set context: Verdance is building an editor-assist feature for designers; we expect bursts of traffic, some private customer data in prompts, and we need to show legal & security that data is handled appropriately. We want a two-week spin up to test live traffic and measure latency.
[00:42] Samir (ML Eng): Technical constraints: we currently run inference with a mix of on-prem GPUs and GCP for training; for prototyping we'd prefer hosted but if latency or residency is an issue we might consider Dedicated or Private.
[00:56] Priya (Security): From security side, main questions are: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS integration, encryption at rest, audit logs, and retention controls.
[01:08] Ethan (AE): Totally. On the PLG side, we offer free credits to get you to first token; typical path is self-serve sign up, SDKs, and a quickstart. Maya, do you want to talk TTFT?
[01:20] Maya (SE): Yep. Time-to-first-token — for most teams it's under an hour if they use our SDK and don't need private connectivity. For a VPC/private deployment it's more setup: VPC peering or on-prem package, so expect a few days to a couple weeks depending on network approvals.
[01:38] Lena (CTO): So hosted could be fast, but we need to be careful about prompts that include customer PII. Can hosted keep prompts encrypted?
[01:45] Maya (SE): We do encryption in transit and at rest by default. For KMS, we support customer-managed keys, and audit logs can be exported to your Splunk or S3 for compliance. There's sometimes confusion — hosted means data touches our control plane, but we have options: Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools, and Private can keep control plane in your VPC.
[02:06] Priya (Security): Does Redwood have SOC2 Type II? And ISO?
[02:10] Ethan (AE): Yes, we have SOC2, and we're working through ISO certs — Maya can share the whitepaper.
[02:17] Maya (SE): I'll attach our SOC2 report and the security pack — it has network diagrams, KMS flow, and retention settings.
[02:24] Samir (ML Eng): On performance: our model workload has short-ish prompts (avg 120 tokens) and we expect 80 RPS burst. How do you recommend we size for that?
[02:35] Maya (SE): For short prompts at 120 tokens, batching helps but if you need single-digit ms latency you want to avoid large batch windows. For hosted, we can tune batching and route to lower-latency instances; Dedicated gives predictability for bursty workloads. For 80 RPS bursts, a small dedicated pool or autoscaling on hosted with concurrency limits should be fine for a pilot.
[03:00] Lena (CTO): Cost is a factor. How do we compare token cost hosted vs dedicated?
[03:05] Ethan (AE): Hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity with commit. For pilots, hosted with credits is usually cheaper short-term; Dedicated has lower per-unit cost at scale but requires a monthly commit. We'll share a cost example sheet.
[03:18] Priya (Security): For the pilot, would you be able to provide a temporary dedicated slice or only hosted?
[03:23] Martha (??) [Speaker label glitch]: I think we could offer a short trial dedicated window for enterprise evals, depending on capacity.
[03:30] Ethan (AE): Sorry, that was me — didn't mute. What I meant — we have options, typically hosted credits are fastest. For dedicated trial we need to align on dates and capacity — Maya can follow up.
[03:42] Maya (SE): For the pilot we'll propose a 2-week hosted sprint with X credits, plus an optional dedicated window if you want to run a controlled benchmark. We'll lay out the test harness: 1) sample prompt set, 2) load pattern (80 RPS bursts), 3) latency and cost KPIs.
[04:00] Samir (ML Eng): Sounds good. We also want to test a quantized model variant — can Redwood serve 4-bit or int8 quantized weights?
[04:08] Maya (SE): Yes, we support quantized variants and will suggest model/quantization combos — there's a tradeoff between latency, cost, and quality. We'll recommend a few based on your prompts.
[04:20] Lena (CTO): Onboarding friction: what integration work for our product engineers?
[04:24] Ethan (AE): Minimal — SDKs for JS/Python and an API key. If you need VPC, that requires network configs and possibly firewall approvals.
[04:32] Priya (Security): For SSO, do you support SAML/SCIM for provisioning?
[04:36] Maya (SE): Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC in the console.
[04:42] Samir (ML Eng): Also curious about KV cache and session handling for chat-like flows (we'll likely keep context per user).
[04:48] Maya (SE): We have KV cache support and memory management; you can control session TTLs to limit cached context for privacy or cost.
[04:58] Lena (CTO): Ok, questions from our procurement/legal — data residency: any options for EU-only processing?
[05:04] Ethan (AE): We have regional endpoints and can route EU traffic to EU regions; for stricter needs, Private deployment in your VPC or on-prem is the option.
[05:12] Priya (Security): On SLAs, what's typical?
[05:15] Maya (SE): Hosted has standard uptime targets; Dedicated comes with stronger SLA commitments and SLOs, plus priority support. We'll attach exact SLA language.
[05:23] Samir (ML Eng): How about rolling out model updates? Can we pin a model version during the pilot?
[05:28] Maya (SE): Yes — you can pin versions and run canary rollouts, A/B tests, or fallback policies. It's part of the console features.
[05:36] Lena (CTO): For the pilot success criteria, we're thinking: latency P95 < 300ms, availability > 99.5% during bursts, and cost per 1k tokens under $X — is that measurable in two weeks?
[05:48] Maya (SE): Yes, with a focused benchmark we can measure those metrics. We'll ensure tracing hooks to map token cost back to routes.
[05:56] Ethan (AE): Ok, next steps — I'll send pricing options and the SOC2 pack. Maya will send a short benchmark plan. Can we get Verdance to share sample prompts and the expected traffic profile?
[06:08] Lena (CTO): We'll send a small prompt set and traffic shape by Friday.
[06:12] Priya (Security): Also need to review the KMS flow doc — send that.
[06:16] Maya (SE): Yep, sending KMS flow and network diagrams.
[06:20] Samir (ML Eng): One more: do you have an example perf spreadsheet or previous benchmark we can look at?
[06:24] Maya (SE): I'll include a sanitized benchmark example.
[06:28] Ethan (AE): Great. Any other questions?
[06:30] Lena (CTO): Not right now. We're keen to move fast.
[06:34] Priya (Security): We'll review the docs and loop in legal.
[06:36] Ethan (AE): Perfect. We'll follow up with the items and schedule the 30-minute pilot kickoff next week.
[06:42] Samir (ML Eng): Thanks everyone.
[06:44] All: Thanks.

Recap / Commitments:
- Redwood: send SOC2 + security pack, pricing/examples, benchmark plan, KMS flow, hacked perf example
- Verdance: send sample prompts, traffic profile, SLO targets
